sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by cell-surface detection assay; OR51E2 showed the most pronounced surface expression among three ORs tested. Functional agonist-response assays not reported in these clips.
sites.rationale: OR51E2 is a GPCR with residues 1–23 extracellular and residues 294–320 intracellular; the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus available for a surface FLAG tag. No residue number is stated in L1/L2, so the junction is topology-derived: insert_after_residue=0 places the tag before M1, 23 residues from TM1 (residues 24–48), well above the ≥3-residue minimum. L3 independently confirms the N-terminal FLAG design on the full-length membrane-anchored receptor, corroborating this position. Full-length OR51E2 with a FLAG epitope tag trafficked robustly to the plasma membrane in HEK293 cells without requiring a Lucy signal peptide or chaperones (PMC5131280). A second study (PMC10580732) explicitly engineered the full-length receptor with an N-terminal influenza hemagglutinin signal sequence followed by a FLAG tag for cryo-EM structural characterization, confirming the N-terminal extracellular placement of the tag on the membrane-anchored receptor.

sources.claim: As shown in Fig. 1d , Flag-tagged full-length constructs encoding OR1J1, OR6A2 and OR51E2 were able to traffic to the cell surface under certain conditions; surface expression of OR51E2 was the most pronounced among the three ORs.

literature_notes: L1 and L2 (same paper, PMC5131280) report surface expression of a Flag-tagged full-length OR51E2 construct but do not state the residue position of the tag. L3 (PMC10580732) explicitly places an HA signal sequence + FLAG at the N-terminus of the full-length receptor for cryo-EM; this confirms the N-terminal extracellular placement and is treated as corroborating the same site. Both converge on a single N-terminal prepend site (insert_after_residue=0). L4 reports a C-terminal miniGαs fusion; the C-terminus is intracellular (residues 294–320) and miniGαs is not an epitope tag, so this is recorded in other_positions only. No ledger line supports an insertion in any of the extracellular loops (ECL1 83–96, ECL2 163–194, ECL3 261–272), so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal miniGαs protein fused to OR51E2 for cryo-EM structural characterization; the C-terminus (residues 294–320) is intracellular per topology landmarks, making this an intracellular fusion, not a surface tag site.
